question: Should FactoryLab build/fork a new local ETL executor, or reuse Duckle as the lower execution foundation?
conclusion: Treat Duckle as the primary lower-layer candidate and stop greenfield executor work until an adapter/fork spike is complete. Default to adapter-first; fork only for measured gaps.

architecture: Rust/Tauri desktop and Rust engine crates
plain pipeline JSON shared across authoring/execution paths
DuckDB engine topologically sorts graphs, lowers stages to SQL and executes them
headless duckle-runner and server mode exist
relevant_capabilities: per-node status, rows, timings and previews
child pipelines and control-flow nodes such as foreach, switch, wait, try/fallback and parallelization
airflow_truth: Duckle documents being driven by Airflow, Dagster or Temporal via CLI or HTTP.
There are currently no official provider packages; an Airflow operator would be a thin integration built on stable CLI/HTTP surfaces.
If Airflow owns the schedule, Duckle recommends leaving Duckle scheduling off to avoid two schedulers owning one cadence.

product_impact.factorylab: Duckle can replace much of the planned generic local ETL/data-flow executor, connector layer, generated-SQL engine, preview/lineage and scheduling substrate.
product_impact.fastapi_fabric: Retain as the Fabric semantics/control/translation API. Do not grow it into a second generic ETL engine unless the Duckle spike proves necessary.
product_impact.fabric_frontend_donor: Retain because the product goal is Fabric/Data Factory learning UX, not a Duckle clone.
product_impact.contoso: No ownership change. Contoso remains the full data-platform/dbt/modeling studio, though FactoryLab can consume Contoso datasets.
product_impact.caselab: Airflow remains here as the deep scheduler-semantics teaching surface; Duckle does not replace fastapiflow.

integration_options.shape: FactoryLab React/Fluent UI -> fastapi-fabric -> FactoryLab-to-Duckle translator -> Duckle pipeline JSON -> duckle-runner/server -> DuckDB/DuckLake
integration_options.reason: Preserves our Fabric-specific UX and semantics while reusing Duckle's expensive execution/observability layer and minimizing fork maintenance.

integration_options.shape: Fork Duckle only after the spike identifies required internals unavailable through documented JSON/CLI/HTTP boundaries.
integration_options.reason: License permits it and the frontend already uses React Flow, but maintaining a large Rust/Tauri/React fork is a real long-term cost.

integration_options.shape: Expand fastapi-fabric into its own full ETL engine.
integration_options.reason: Avoid unless Duckle cannot satisfy core requirements; it would duplicate substantial proven functionality.

spike_acceptance: Translate and execute a basic Copy pipeline.
Translate and execute a Source -> Select/Filter -> DuckLake Sink data flow.
Return per-node status, rows, timings and error details into FactoryLab.
Obtain data preview and generated SQL/plan.
Obtain lineage or document any API gap.
Exercise one Duckle ctl.* control node.
List exact Fabric semantics that require fastapi-fabric-only handling.
no_go_rules: Do not call Duckle Microsoft Fabric or Apache Airflow.
Do not use Duckle scheduling and Airflow scheduling simultaneously for the same owned cadence.
Do not move Airflow teaching ownership from CaseLab to FactoryLab.
Do not expose Duckle dbt capability as a reason to move dbt product ownership out of Contoso.
Do not fork Duckle merely to change colors or labels.
